full_judgment: 2. The petitioner stated that she purchased the land measuring. 70 acres with a two-storied residential house at holding No. 10/1, Toyenbee Circular Road, Dhaka pertaining to C.S. plot No. 33, R.S. plot Nos. 2411. 2412 and 2413 of C.S. khatian No. 6147(U) and R.S . .Khatian No.390 of mouza Shahar Dhaka in 1951 to the extent of .66 acres and in 1955 to the extent of .6 acres by registered sale deeds and since then she had been enjoying and performing acts of ownership and possession by residing in the house, paying rents and taxes to the Government and other local authorities. The husband of the petitioner was a politician belonging to the Muslim League. He was out of Bangladesh at the time of liberation of the entry. The petitioner's house at 10/1, Toyenbee Circular Road, Dhaka and her other properties were attached by the Government of Bangladesh as collaborator's properties under the Bangladesh Cola- bora tors (Special Tribunal) Order, 1972 (P.O. No.8 of 1972) on the misinformation that these properties might belong to Mr. Wahiduzzaman, husband of the petitioner. In view of the order of attachment the petitioner had to vacate the said house and thereafter an investigation was made at the instance of the petitioner with regard to the right, title, interest and possession of the said house. The Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Bangladesh, the respondent No. 3, by a Memo dated 9.10.75 released the said property along with the petitioner's another house at 2, Nanda LalDuua Lane, Dhaka from attachment. The release order is Annexure B. The properties belonging to Mr. Wahiduzzaman were also released by the Government. His citizenship was restored and he died in Bangladesh in 1976: The petitioner received delivery of possession of the said property and afterwards leased it out to the Parjatan Corporation vide lease deed dated 9.12.76, Annexure C. The lease was terminated in 1980 and since then the petitioner has been enjoying peaceful and undisturbed possession r the said property through three of her sons Habib' zaman, Rashiduzzaman and Sinku Akramuzzai who have jointly set up an office for their various businesses in the said house and have also been using part of it in storing equipment’s and other merchandise connected with their businesses. The petitioner has been paying rent regularly to the Government Acquired Estates. The said property has never been declared or treated as abandoned property nor taken possession of by the Government in any manner under the President's Order No. 16 of 1972. The petitioner was surprised to see the public notice dated 28.4.R6 published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extra-Ordinary on 28.4.86 under-the provisions of -vs . Section 5(1 )(a) of the Abandoned Building (Supplementary provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No.LIV of 1985) (Annexure E) wherein the petitioner's said house has been included in the said notice as an abandoned property the possession of which has been taken as abandoned property under P.O.No. 16 of 1972. The petitioner asserts that she is in possession of the said house and the respondents or any- body else on their behalf have not taken possession or the said property nor served any notices to include the said house in the list of.abandoned properties. The petitioner served a notice of demand of justice on 31.7.86, but the demand having not been complied with the petitioner thereafter obtained thepresent Rule.
